title: Memory, context, control
intro: The foundation the whole course builds on: give Claude Code memory, manage its context, and keep your hands on the controls.

steps.title: Project memory
steps.body:
**`/init`** scans the codebase and writes **CLAUDE.md** — important commands, architecture, coding style — automatically loaded into context on every launch.

**`#`** appends a memory in one keystroke. The course's first two additions: *"use uv to run python files or add any dependencies"* (the moment Claude used pip), and the vector database's two collections with their full schemas.

steps.title: Context is a budget
steps.body:
| Control | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/clear` | wipe conversation history |
| `/compact` | summarize it in place |
| `ESC` | interrupt and redirect mid-flight |
| `ESC ESC` | rewind to an earlier point |

> [!tip] Clear between unrelated tasks; compact when the task continues but history bloats. Interrupting early beats arguing with a finished wrong answer.

steps.title: Precision inputs
steps.body: **`@file`** pins exact files into a prompt (`@backend/search_tools.py`) — no guessing where changes live. **`!command`** runs bash inline (`!pwd`). Together with plan mode, they make prompts *addressable*: files named, commands run, plans reviewed before code.

steps.title: Explore before you modify
steps.body:
Lesson 2 spends its entire session asking questions — codebase overview, how documents are chunked (down to the sentence-boundary regex), how the two ChromaDB collections differ, how sessions persist — and correcting Claude's model with `#` as it goes.

Only after the map is right does any change get requested.

recap:
**/init → correct with # → manage context → explore first.**

- CLAUDE.md is auto-loaded project memory; # patches it the moment an error repeats.
- /clear between tasks, /compact within them, ESC to redirect, ESC ESC to rewind.
- @files and !commands make prompts precise.
- Questions are cheaper than reverts.
